Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:25: And so too one must consider and know that according to the path through which things were created, so their aspect and form indicate. Such as the rose, which has thirteen petals and five strong petals, as Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, Bereshit 1a): one must understand and consider the divine wisdom that created it through the power of a particular path, and therefore its outward action was necessarily produced in this number of petals. And there is a rose with five petals, as explained in the Tikkunim (71a), indicating the five letters of "Elohim," as Rashbi explains there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:26: And along these lines, concerning the candle, Rashbi explains (Zohar, Bereshit 50b) that it indicates the secret of supernal unity; in these words: but come and see, whoever wishes to know the wisdom of holy unity should observe the flame that rises from a coal or from a burning lamp, and so on. And he explains there that the rising flame, which is white light, hints at Tiferet, and the coal, whose color is blue, corresponds to the Shechinah, which is fire. And at the end of his words, I found in manuscript a pleasant matter, in these words: and upon the white light rests above it a concealed light that surrounds it, and this is a supernal secret - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:27: And along these lines, concerning fish, which have no covering over the eye - to show the supernal aspect they hint at, which is "an open eye" - as explained in the Idra of Naso (Zohar 129b); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:28: And so too the black rooster that crows at midnight to awaken people to the service of the Creator - its matter is explained (there, Parashat Vayechi 218a), and we copied his text in the Gate of Fear, chapter 12; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:29: And along these lines, for other things in the world, one must discern in them the secret of supernal wisdom - and so Rashbi explains (Shemot 15a), in these words: Rabbi Akiva said to him, it implies that everything the Holy One, blessed be He, did is to learn abundant wisdom from it, as it is said (Proverbs 16:4), "the LORD has made everything for His own purpose." Rabbi Elazar said, from here, as it is written (Genesis 1:31), "and God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good" - what is "very" [me'od]? To learn from it abundant supernal wisdom. Rabbi Yehuda said: what is written (Ecclesiastes 7:14), "God has made even this corresponding to that"? Just as the firmament, so the Holy One, blessed be He, made on earth, and all of them hint at what is above - to the extent relevant here. And there they explain the kinds of fruits and trees, and their hints - such as the walnut, which has four parts, hinting at the four river-heads, which are the secret of the Chariot - and the rest, see there; and in order not to elaborate too much, we did not copy his whole text.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:30: And along these lines, the discerning reader must discern in every work of creation and find the bond and cause between the caused thing and its cause - and through this he will know and recognize that there is one Creator for everything, and all are given from one Shepherd. Especially when he further knows that the work of creation is expounded both above and below - above, in the supernal spiritual beings, and below, in this world. And this is "bereishit" [two "reishit," i.e., "beginning"] - two "beginnings," one above and one below, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:31: It follows from this that this world, although it has become physical below, has a spiritual counterpart above, in its generalities and particulars - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Beshalach 48b), in these words: come and see, corresponding to what is above, there is below; corresponding to what is below, there is in the sea; corresponding to what is above, there is above, in the supernal sea; corresponding to what is above, there is below; corresponding to what is below, there is in the lower sea - the body of that sea, as we have already established, connecting them: length and breadth, head and arms, hairs and body, all as needed, and all called by its name. And correspondingly, below, the lower sea likewise has a head of the sea, and arms of the sea, and a body of the sea - to this point. And along these lines Rashbi explains (there, Parashat Shemot 20a), which we have not copied, so as not to elaborate.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:32: And the reason it is necessary that everything above have a counterpart below is that existing things are like a seal stamped one from another, down to the descent of things into this physicality - for first there is Adam of Atzilut, the generality of existing things in their fineness, and it is stamped upon Adam of Beriah, and so from Beriah to Yetzirah to Asiyah. And therefore it is necessary that in Asiyah there be the image of Adam [man], and therefore he says that the sea has hairs and arms.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:33: And along these lines, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (there, Pekudei 231b) that the making of the Tabernacle was like the making of heaven and earth, and likewise the lower Garden of Eden is a seal of the upper world and the lower world; in these words: it is written, "in the beginning God created the heavens and the earth," and they have established that everything was made in this manner in the Tabernacle - He made it corresponding to the lower world and corresponding to the upper world, and all His works were made corresponding to what is above - so too the Tabernacle, all its workings are like the workings in the manner of the upper world. This is the secret: all the workings of the Tabernacle are all the workings and repairs of above and below, in order to make the Shechinah dwell in the world, in the supernal dwellings and in the lower dwellings. Correspondingly, in the lower Garden of Eden, it is in the manner of above and the manner of below - all the forms and all the images of the world are all there - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:34: And so too, from this we understand that the measurements of the Temple's construction were all made in a supernal configuration, hinting at the measurements of the supernal Temple - as it is written in Chronicles (I Chronicles 28:11), "and David gave to Solomon his son the plan of the porch and its houses, and its treasuries and its upper chambers and its inner chambers," and so on (ibid. 28:19), "all this, said David, the LORD made me understand in writing, by His hand upon me, all the works of this plan." It follows that all these existing things are the pattern of these - the lower ones the image and pattern of the upper ones.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:35: And along these lines, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain that the earth has the whole configuration of man; in these words (Midrash Zuta, Ecclesiastes 1:4): "but the earth endures forever" (Ecclesiastes 1:4) - Reish Lakish said, everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in man, He created in the earth. Man has a head, and the earth has a head, as it is said (Proverbs 8:26), "and the head [rosh] of the dust of the world." Man has eyes, and the earth has eyes, as it is said (Exodus 10:15), "and it covered the eye of the whole earth." Man has ears, and the earth has ears, as it is said (Isaiah 1:2), "and give ear [ha'azini], O earth." Man eats, and the earth eats, as it is said (Numbers 13:33 [13:32]), "a land that eats up its inhabitants." Man drinks, and the earth drinks, as it is said (Deuteronomy 11:11), "it drinks water of the rain of heaven." Man trembles [convulses], and the earth trembles, as it is said (II Samuel 22:8), "and the earth shook and trembled." Man becomes drunk, and the earth becomes drunk, as it is said (Isaiah 24:20), "the earth shall stagger like a drunken man." Man vomits, and the earth vomits, as it is said (Leviticus 18:25), "and the land vomited out its inhabitants." Man has hands, and the earth likewise, as it is said (Genesis 34:21), "and the land, behold, it is wide-handed [broad]." Man has a navel, and the earth likewise, as it is said (Ezekiel 38:12), "who dwells at the navel of the earth." Man has thighs [flanks], and the earth likewise, as it is said (Jeremiah 31:7), "and I will gather them from the flanks of the earth." Man has feet, and the earth likewise, as it is said, "and the earth endures forever" and maintains its post - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:36: And along these lines, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain, brought in the Yalkut (Tehillim, section 672), at the beginning of the psalm "the heavens declare" (Psalms 19:1-2), that the sea and the heavens have [bodily features], and although not all are mentioned, hinting at all the limbs: it says the sea has eyes, as it is said (Psalms 114:3), "the sea saw, and fled." And it has hands, as it is said (ibid. 104:25), "this sea, great and wide-handed." And the heavens have a heart, as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:32), "to the heart of the heavens." And likewise the sea, as it is said (Exodus 15:8), "the depths congealed in the heart of the sea." The heavens have a mouth, as it is said (Psalms 19:2), "the heavens declare [i.e., speak]." And likewise the earth, as it is said (Numbers 16:32), "and the earth opened its mouth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:37: And concerning all the limbs mentioned of the sea, the heavens, and the earth, it says in the Midrash (Yalkut, there) that they are not visible to creatures, but only to the Holy One, blessed be He - and we must say that this is the reality of the spiritual Asiyah [level of Action], which is not attained by lower human beings, and within its spiritual reality is hinted the mentioned limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:38: Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla, peace be upon him, wrote, in his commentary on the Chariot of Ezekiel, a pleasant matter concerning contemplation, and I have seen fit to copy his words, peace be upon him, in these words: and behold, the Blessed Name, since He created the angels in the utmost perfection and inwardness, although we cannot show the hidden forms to the sensory eye, the form of the stars is shown, to understand from them the concealed forms. And behold, the sun and the moon, both of them, are clear witnesses, indicating to us the supernal, hidden, and concealed things within the secrets of the supernal chariots - and this is the secret of (Genesis 1:16), "and God made the two great lights" - in truth, they were great lights to illuminate the earth, to illuminate our eyes, we who dwell on the earth, to understand from them the secret of several supernal mysteries in the order of the intellectual levels, and above, in the secret of the sefirot, and in the secret of the reality of the Blessed Name and His unity. And behold, all the configurations, supernal and lower, hidden and revealed, are all patterns for the secrets of the supernal Chariot, and from the sensory and comprehensible we can understand and know those hidden and concealed things - and this is the secret of (Isaiah 40:26), "lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:39: And he further writes below, concerning the image of man in this, that all the orders of the Chariot are all arranged in the order of the form of man - for there are camps in the order of the Chariot called by the name "gate," and some called "ears," and some called "eyes," and so on, and some further called "feet," and likewise all the other forms of limbs in the configuration of man; and each one of these supernal camps is the secret of that action for which the limb is designated, and all these camps, when joined together as one, are called "Adam," and they are all thrones for the great Blessed Name, and He, blessed be He, rules over them all, and He is within them like the soul within the body, and from Him they receive their flow and their endurance - to this point, summarizing his intent. And along these lines Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Tikkunim (28a, 130a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:40: And along these mentioned discourses, they explain in the Zohar (Toldot 134b) that the Torah, man, and the world are one matter; in these words: come and see, whoever strives in the Torah sustains the world and sustains every single deed in its proper repair, as is fitting; and there is no single limb standing in a person that does not have its counterpart, a creature, in the world - for just as a person is divided into limbs, and they all stand as levels, set in order one upon another, and when they are all set in order, behold, one body - so too the world, all those creatures are limbs upon limbs, standing one upon another, and when they are all set in order, behold, literally one body. And all this is in the manner of the Torah, for the Torah is all limbs and sections, standing one upon another, and when they are all set in order, they become one body - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:41: And because we are not careful in our language to mention, above, a body and the form of man and the like, matters of body and physicality - and this matter is very far from believable, since He, blessed be He, is not a body and has no form, so His throne and His garment cannot be joined or designated with images of the body, Heaven forfend - but all of these are only designations for hidden things and concealed names, all of them holy names. And whoever has read the book Brit Menuchah will see something of this, although it did not speak of Atzilut - it designated all the limbs with holy names, calling the lungs by the Name of 72, and the liver by the Name of 42, and so on for all the other limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:42: And along these lines, Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla writes in the introduction to Sefer HaOrah. And he further writes, in his commentary on the Chariot, in these words: and I state a general rule to you, and guard it everywhere: let it never occur to you, wherever you find me referring to a term like "hand" or "foot" or other limbs I have selected for it, that this means the form of a hand or the form of a foot, or the essence of a hand or the essence of a foot - for the matter is not so, not a little and not a lot. Rather, the matter is only in the manner of naming, not in the manner of essence, substance, and forms - for the forms of the Chariot are grasped only in supernal visions, by prophets and seers. Indeed, there are some levels of angels who clothe themselves in a garment close to the human eye, and this is a known matter in the powers of clothing. And know and believe that each of the parts of the Chariot called "hand" and "foot" and "ear" and "eye" and the like - all of these have an inner, supernal source, like a flowing spring, and it flows into each of the parts of the Chariot what it can sustain - each according to its kind and matter, so is its grasp and reception; how is this so? This one's vision is not like that one's vision, and everything is emanated upon them from the Blessed Name in the secret of the ten sefirot, through which the intent of all existing things and their endurance is completed. And those ten sefirot, in which is the place of all existence in the world - no one can know their essence and matter, and they do not enter into any comparison, measure, or knowledge of any existing thing among all existing things - and so the prophet proclaims (Isaiah 40:25), "to whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal? says the Holy One." And whoever thinks in his mind that they have a boundary or a measure or a comparison is among those of little faith, comparable to one who has no God, and worships his own reflection - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:43: And in the words of the Rabbi, of blessed memory, there is enough to negate physicality from these matters - that everything mentioned in the Torah and the Prophets, such as (Isaiah 34:6), "the sword of the LORD is filled with blood," is all a parable. And so it is explained in Parashat Shemot (Zohar 19b), on this verse: Rabbi Abba said, this sword is the judgment that He performs, as it is written (I Chronicles 21:16), "and David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between the earth and the heaven, with his sword drawn in his hand" - was there literally a drawn sword in the angel's hand? Rather, permission was given to execute judgment. If so, what is "and he returned his sword into its sheath"? Rabbi Abba said, that the judgment returned to the master of the judgment, and the permission to the one to whom the permission belongs - to the extent relevant here. And if in this matter our Rabbis, of blessed memory, stripped away physicality, how much more so higher and higher above - rather, certainly everything mentioned in the Torah, "the eyes of the LORD," "the ears of the LORD," is all a parable for providence or for hearing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:44: And along these lines, there is a second distinction within the general category of the world and the creatures in it - that they were all created from four elements; this indicates that one Creator brought them into being through His great Name, which has four letters, which are the root of the four elements, as explained in the Tikkunim (68b), whose text we will copy below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:45: And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Va'era 23b), in these words: Rabbi Shimon said, come and see, four are the first ones, the secret of faith, and they are the fathers of all the worlds and the secret of the supernal, holy Chariot, and they are fire, wind, water, and earth. These are the supernal secret, and these are the fathers of all the worlds, the fathers of everything; and from them go forth gold, silver, copper, and iron, and beneath these are other metals resembling them, in the manner of these. Come and see: fire, wind, water, and earth - these are the first ones and the roots of above and below, and the lower and upper ones stand upon them; and these are the four, corresponding to the four directions of the world, and they stand in these four: north, south, east, and west - these are the four directions of the world, and they stand in these four: fire to the north side, wind to the east side, water to the south side, earth to the west side. These four are bound within these four, and they are all one; and these make the four metals, which are gold, silver, copper, and iron - behold, they are twelve, and they are all one - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:46: And when a person discerns this matter with his intellect, he will recognize his Creator from the side of His actions - whether from the side of the mentioned metals, or from the side of man himself, composed of the four elements, as explained above. And so too, from this, one may discern the secret of precious stones and pearls - some whose color is white, whose property is grace and kindness, and some whose color is red, whose property is to cast dread - and everything comes from the supernal root of the supernal attributes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:47: And he further explains in the discourse there that we find the north moist, having water, and the south hot and dry - and he says that the Holy One, blessed be He, did this in order to bind the winds of the world to one another, just as the supernal attributes are blended above, south within north and north within south; and so is their matter below, in this world - that the waters, which are in the south, go to the north, and the fire of the north enters the south - and this is the secret of the Binding of Isaac, explained in the Zohar in the commentary on the passage (Vayera 119b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:48: Further, concerning matters of contemplating the creation of the world, they elaborate in the Zohar (Vayikra 9b), and I have seen fit to copy some of his text, not all, because of its length, in these words: Rabbi Yehuda opened, "and God said, let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters" - come and see: at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created seven firmaments above, He created seven lands below, seven seas, seven rivers, seven days, seven weeks, seven years, seven times [seven] - seven thousand years the world will endure, and the Holy One, blessed be He, [rests] in the seventh of everything.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:49: Seven heavens above, and in each and every one, stars and constellations and servants that serve in each and every firmament, and in all of them, these chariots [stand] one upon another, to accept upon themselves the yoke of the kingdom of their Master. And in all the firmaments there are chariots and servants, differing one from another, one upon another - some with six wings, some with four wings, some with four faces, some with two faces, some with one; and some are blazing fire, some water, some wind - this is what is written (Psalms 104:4), "who makes His angels winds, His ministers a blazing fire" - and all these firmaments, one upon another, are like the layers of onions, these below and these above; and every single firmament goes and trembles from dread of its Master - by His word they travel and by His word they stand, and above them all is the Holy One, blessed be He, who carries everything with His power and strength.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:50: Correspondingly, there are seven lands below, and all of them are inhabited, except that these are above and these below, and the Land of Israel is above them all, and Jerusalem is above all the inhabited world; and we, who dwell in the south, have seen in the first books, in the book of Adam, that all those lands are thus divided, all found below corresponding to those firmaments above, these upon these and these upon these, and between each land and land is a firmament separating between this one and that one, and therefore all the lands are distinguished by their names, and among them are the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom. And among them there are creatures differing from one another, corresponding to those chariots above - some with two faces, some with four, some with one - and the appearance of these is not like those, and should you say... and so on [text continues but is truncated].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:51: And at the end they say, in these words: Rabbi Nehora Sava set sail on the great sea, and the sea grew turbulent, and all those who were in the boat were lost; a miracle happened to him, and he descended through known paths in the heart of the sea, and came out beneath the sea into a certain inhabited region, and he saw creatures there, all of them small, and they were praying a prayer, and he did not know what they were saying; a miracle happened to him and he ascended. He said: happy are the righteous who strive in Torah and know the hidden things of the supernal secrets; woe to those who dispute their words and do not believe. From that day on, whenever he would come to the study house and speak a word of Torah, he would weep. They said to him: why do you weep? He said to them: because I transgressed against the faith of the words of the Sages, and I fear the judgment of that world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:52: And when a person considers the creation of the world and its greatness, and the great sea and the creatures in it, as it is said (Psalms 104:25), "this sea, great and wide-handed, in which are creeping things innumerable" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say (Mishnah, end of Kiddushin) that most sailors are pious, because they see the wonders of the LORD in the great sea, as it is written (Psalms 107:24), "these see the works of the LORD, and His wonders in the deep." And in what the LORD rebuked Job, saying to him (Job 38:16), "have you entered into the springs of the sea, or walked in the recesses of the deep?" and so on, "have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Declare, if you know it all" (ibid. 38:18); "have you entered the storehouses of the snow?" (ibid. 38:22); "who shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble" (ibid. 9:6) - which is the matter of earthquakes, one of the great signs showing the creation, and the reason for earthquakes is explained in Parashat Shemot (Zohar 17b) - and the other particulars mentioned there - certainly he will recognize the greatness of the Creator and know that He created everything, that He created everything for His honor, and he will subjugate himself to His service and love Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:53: And among the particulars of contemplation is what Rabbi Yehuda mentions at the beginning of the discourse we copied - "He created seven firmaments," and so on, "seven seas," and so on, "and the Holy One, blessed be He, in the seventh of everything" - for the Holy One, blessed be He, chose for Himself the sevenths, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain in the Midrash (Yalkut Shimoni, Shmuel, remez 94), which Rabbi Menachem Recanati, of blessed memory, copies in his commentary.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:54: And it is fitting that a person discern this very matter, found in the mouths of all seventy nations, in seventy languages, that the name "Shabbat" has not changed in any language - rather, all call the seventh day "Shabbat." And the reason is that Shabbat indicates the renewal of the world, and that the Holy One, blessed be He, created it in seven days and rested and ceased on the seventh - therefore it did not change, so that all would recognize that there is one Creator for everything. And of this matter of contemplation is the Sambatyon River, which flows all six days and rests on the seventh day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:55: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain another proof for Shabbat - this in the Midrash Tehillim, on the psalm (Psalms 19:2), "the heavens declare the glory of God," on the verse (Proverbs 16:4), "the LORD has made everything for His own purpose [la'anoto, "for its answer/testimony"]" - it says, in these words: another interpretation: "for its testimony," along the lines of what is said (Exodus 20:13 [20:16]), "you shall not answer [testify] falsely against your neighbor," and it is written (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and my friends." Rabbi Abahu said: there are two things the nations of the world do not deny: that the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world in six days, and that He revives the dead. How so? A person goes and digests his food all the days of the week, and it digests; but on Shabbat it does not digest - and an animal, even on a weekday, does not digest [in the sense of purification for eating a limb from a living animal, or some related halachic point], because it will not live in the future to come. Behold, "everything the LORD has made [is] for His testimony" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:56: Further, concerning the matter of contemplation, is what the prophet says (Isaiah 40:26), "lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these: He who brings out their host by number, He calls them all by name, by the greatness of His might, and because He is strong in power, not one is missing." And in the Zohar (Bereshit 1b), Rashbi, peace be upon him, says that Elijah came to him and said: Rabbi, do you know what "who has created these" means? I said to him: these are the heavens and their hosts, the work of the Holy One, blessed be He, which a person must gaze upon and bless Him for, as it is written (Psalms 8:4), "when I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers," and so on, "O LORD, our Master, how mighty is Your name in all the earth" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:57: And Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, Pekudei 231b), further explains this verse and elaborates more on it, in these words: rather, "lift up your eyes on high" - whoever wishes to gaze upon and know the deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He, should raise his eyes above and see how many forces and how many camps of deeds, differing from one another, greater than one another; and then, when you see and ask and say, who created these? "Who created these" - we have already established the secret of "who created these," that that place stands on high, hidden and concealed and unknown, and always stands to be asked, because that place is not revealed. "Who brings out by number their host" - what is "brings out"? Rather, because that place is hidden and concealed, it brings out everything in the secret of the sound that comes forth from the shofar - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:58: And further on he explains that there is firmament and stars, one above the other, down to the descent of the matter to this firmament and these stars visible to our eyes; and in these words: come and see, those stars that are below stand by a drawing drawn from the supernal secret, because everything stands in the supernal image - and we have already established this. So all those stars and constellations of the height of the firmament all stand to guide the world below through them, and from there they spread until levels stand within those stars below, for none of them stand by their own authority at all - and we have already established this - and they all stand by the authority of what is above; and therefore it is written (Isaiah 47:13), "let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up and save you" - and everything is by authority, as has been said - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:59: And although the plain sense of the verse "lift up your eyes on high," and so on, "who brings out by number their host," refers to the creation of the heavens and the hosts of stars, which go out and come in by number and by name - nevertheless, there [elsewhere] it is explained in the Zohar (Bereshit 2b) that "bereishit" refers to Israel, who have six hundred thousand souls, and not one is ever lacking from six hundred thousand - and this indicates that they are the pattern of the supernal Chariot, which has six hundred thousand aspects, as known to those who know this wisdom. And so I have heard from astronomers, that all the stars number six hundred thousand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:60: There are further matters concerning contemplation - when one discerns the particular matters of the world, he will find them all hinting at supernal matters, and there is no need to elaborate on them. Further, I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, a general matter of contemplation encompassing all herbs and all seeds and trees - that you will find that oil comes from all of them, and this indicates the secret of wisdom spreading into all creatures, as it says (Psalms 104:24), "You have made them all in wisdom." And so he should consider the matter of thunder, which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain, on the verse (Ecclesiastes 3:14), "and God has done it, that men should fear before Him" - that it was created only to straighten the crookedness of the heart - and we copied this in the Gate of Fear, chapter 11. And so too several other things, such as earthquakes and the roaring of the lion, and so on; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:61: And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 3) that one must contemplate all the things in the world - such as the eternal motion of the celestial spheres, and the flowing of the rivers' waters from the springs, night and day without resting or stopping, and the descent of rains, and the blowing of the winds, and the emergence of the infant from the womb - for all these indicate the wonders of the Creator, His mercy, and the abundance of His providence over His creatures; and one who ignores contemplating these matters is like a blind man, and therefore one must open the eyes of his intellect to contemplate matters in order to observe and know the wonders of the LORD. This is a summary of his intent, and he elaborates further - and whoever wishes to see it, the book is before him; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:62: Among the things one must discern, in the matter of creation, in the working of the world, is when he considers the working of day and night, which is one of the things created in the work of creation, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain; and it is known that the measure of day and the measure of night have their secret above, in Atzilut - that it is the governance of judgment and the governance of mercy. And therefore King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 104:20-22), "You appoint darkness, and it is night, in which all the beasts of the forest creep forth; the young lions roar after their prey, and seek their food from God" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say that this is in the measure of night, as Rashbi explains in Parashat Bamidbar (119b), concerning the matter of "and God is indignant every day" - and this is because the measure of night is what sustains these spirits, which it needs for the repair of the world, along the lines of (Genesis 29:3), "and they would put the stone back upon the mouth of the well," as explained in Parashat Vayetze (Zohar 152a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:63: And it says, "the sun rises, they gather themselves together" - because then the governance of mercy rules, and all those forces enter into the aperture of the great abyss, as explained in the Zohar in several places; and support for this is (Genesis 44:3), "as soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys." And this matter is visibly apparent in the matter of the sick, for at night their illness grows heavier, and by day, especially until midday, the illness eases from them, because then Chesed rules.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:64: And this is what the verse says (Deuteronomy 4:39), "and you shall know this day, and consider it in your heart, that the LORD, He is God" - the explanation being: when you know the secret of "day" - for "day" without qualification is [both] day and night, as it says (Genesis 1:8 [1:5]), "and there was evening and there was morning, one day," throughout the entire work of creation - you will know that "the LORD, He is God" - that they are the governance of mercy, the secret of YHVH, and the governance of judgment, in the secret of "Elohim" - the two of them one unity, just as it is impossible for night without day, or day without night.
